rq: joint identification of raw-language equivalence and latent intervention-target partition
result: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (Annals of Statistics 2009) establish that a finite hidden class and its class-conditional distributions across three paired conditionally independent observed view groups are generically identifiable up to one simultaneous class-label permutation when the Kruskal-rank condition holds. Therefore class-level language-to-causal coupling is not universally non-identifiable and cannot be claimed as open in this regime. The remaining RQ must go beyond finite three-view latent-class assumptions by addressing sequential dependence, context, unknown class count, polysemy, intervention uncertainty, rank failure, and the distinction between relative coupling and externally oriented semantics. Two-view factorization, duplicated class-conditional rows, and conditional-independence violations remain explicit non-identifiability boundaries. No paper-specific official code was identified; numerical reproduction was not started.
primary_prior_art: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes, Identifiability of Parameters in Latent Structure Models with Many Observed Variables, Annals of Statistics 2009
